plans.note: Section 15 is titled 'Limitation of Garman's Liability' — likely one-sided in the vendor's favour. Check for a meaningful cap figure (fees paid), mutuality, and carve-outs for the IP indemnity (sec-13) and confidentiality breach (sec-14).

Section 13 provides an IP indemnity from Garman; verify scope (defence, settlement control, no fee-only remedy) and add cover for Garman's own misconduct. Confirm sec-15 does not cap or gut the indemnity.

No non-compete heading; a software licence of this type rarely restricts our business lines. Scan sec-3 (Restrictions on Use) and sec-20 (General Matters) for any covenant not to use competing routing products.
No exclusivity section apparent. Check the licence grant (sec-2), maintenance (sec-10) and fees (sec-11) for sole-source or exclusive-supplier language on maintenance or future modules.
No pricing-parity clause expected; review sec-11 (Fees) and sec-10 maintenance uplift terms for any obligation running against us, and note MFN in our favour would be welcome.
Section 19 (Non-Solicitation of Employees) is the operative clause — confirm mutuality, a term of no more than 12 months post-termination, and a general-advertising/unsolicited-applicant carve-out.

Section 17 (Term and Termination) is primary; sec-7/sec-8 (Option to Reject Software) give an early exit path. Check whether we have convenience termination on notice without penalty and that Garman cannot terminate mid-term other than for material breach.
Maintenance term and renewal mechanics likely sit in sec-10 and sec-17, with pricing in sec-11. Verify any auto-renewal has a short non-renewal notice window for us and a capped fee uplift.

Governing law and venue almost certainly sit in sec-20 (General Matters). Confirm the law is NY/DE/CA or England and Wales and that disputes go to courts, not offshore arbitration — relevant given the US/UK cross-border parties.

Assignment clause expected in sec-20; licence transfer limits may also appear in sec-2/sec-3. Ensure we may assign to affiliates and successors (including on change of control) without consent, and that Garman has no termination right on our change of control.

Vendor retains software IP (sec-2/sec-3), but confirm we own our data and any converted data (sec-4 data conversion), that no assignment of our IP or feedback runs to Garman, and check escrow (sec-16) and confidentiality (sec-14) alignment.

Section 2 grants the licence with defined terms/Authorized Locations in sec-1. Confirm the grant is perpetual/irrevocable (not revocable at will) and extends to our affiliates, outsourcers and contractors; sec-3 restrictions may need conforming.

Usage-verification rights, if any, would sit with the use restrictions in sec-3 or in sec-20. If present, limit to once annually, on reasonable written notice, during business hours and at Garman's cost.
No liquidated damages heading; check sec-11 for late-payment interest or penalty charges payable by us, and sec-10 for whether support failures give us credits (which we welcome).

Section 12 (Specifications and Warranty) is primary, supported by acceptance testing (sec-6) and rejection rights (sec-7). Check warranty duration runs a meaningful period from acceptance with repair/replace plus refund as a real remedy.
No insurance section in the outline; likely absent. Given Garman personnel install on-site and handle our data (sec-4, sec-9), propose a standard insurance covenant in sec-20.
No standalone commitment clause, but check sec-11 (Fees) and sec-10 for minimum maintenance periods, non-cancellable annual fees or licence-count minimums tied to schedules in sec-1.

Termination consequences in sec-17/sec-8 likely require return or destruction of software rather than giving us exit help; escrow (sec-16) is only a partial substitute. Expect to add data return and transition assistance obligations and confirm survival in sec-18.
